objections.claim_attacked: observation: metal1 usage 1043.75% alongside prior_state's claim that OBS blocks M1–M5 leaving only M6 free
objections.objection: If M1–M5 are genuinely blocked by RAM OBS over the macros, a metal1 usage figure over 1000% for the design as a whole is plausible only as a localized/edge statistic (e.g., overflow concentrated in the narrow free channels around the RAMs) rather than a chip-wide average; the record does not clarify whether this figure is global or localized, so its scale is asserted without the qualification needed to judge it consistent with the OBS-blocking hypothesis.

objections.claim_attacked: chosen_intervention: 'No single code intervention was adopted' paired with hypothesis listing multiple specific candidate root causes as if diagnosis narrowed to them
objections.objection: The hypothesis field presents several distinct, sometimes competing explanations (resource-accounting mismatch, macro placement/halos, RAM CLASS, density) but the thread explicitly never adjudicates between them per the gaps field; treating these as 'the hypothesis' risks implying a settled explanatory chain when the record shows an open disagreement that was never resolved to a single cause.

mechanism_check: N-D — no intervention was adopted in the thread, so there is no chosen mechanism to evaluate against post_state; the episode itself is a diagnosis-only record rather than a fix-outcome record.
evidence_check: ASSERT — post_state is a participant's qualitative conclusion ('groute map is wrong, without macros this should be easily routable') with no re-measured congestion, overflow, or DRC numbers given after any change.
attribution_check: SUPPORTS — the quote is attributed to a named participant (maliberty) with a date, and its content directly supports the record's closing framing that the design's extreme density makes routability doubtful.
missing_from_story: Any resolution or decision on which of the listed candidate causes (resource-accounting semantics, macro halos, RAM CLASS, density) was actually responsible, since the thread leaves this explicitly unresolved.
